es: Reconocer si un mensaje es formal o informal a partir de sus marcas (saludo, petición, léxico, contracciones y cierre).

teaching.en: Dear Mr Hill, I would be grateful if you could arrange for the heater in my flat to be repaired at your earliest convenience.
teaching.es: Estimado señor Hill, le agradecería que dispusiera la reparación de la calefacción de mi piso a la mayor brevedad posible.
teaching.explanationEs: Formal: Dear + apellido, would be grateful if you could y pasiva (to be repaired); at your earliest convenience = cuanto antes.
segments: Dear Mr Hill, I would be grateful if you could arrange for
the heater in my flat to be repaired at your earliest convenience.
teaching.audioText: Dear Mr Hill, I would be grateful if you could arrange for the heater in my flat to be repaired at your earliest convenience.

teaching.en: Hey Sam, the heater has packed up again, so can you sort it out before the weekend? Cheers, mate!
teaching.es: Oye, Sam, la calefacción se ha estropeado otra vez, ¿puedes arreglarla antes del fin de semana? ¡Gracias, colega!
teaching.explanationEs: Informal: Hey, packed up y sort out (verbos frasales), can you… y cierre con Cheers.
segments: Hey Sam, the heater has packed up again, so can
you sort it out before the weekend? Cheers, mate!
teaching.audioText: Hey Sam, the heater has packed up again, so can you sort it out before the weekend? Cheers, mate!

teaching.en: Even a polite greeting can give away the register: Dear Mr Hill sounds formal, whereas Hiya sounds casual and friendly.
teaching.es: Incluso un saludo educado puede delatar el registro: Dear Mr Hill suena formal, mientras que Hiya suena coloquial y cercano.
teaching.explanationEs: Give away = revelar sin querer; el saludo es la primera pista del registro.
segments: Even a polite greeting can give away the register: Dear
Mr Hill sounds formal, whereas Hiya sounds casual and friendly.
teaching.audioText: Even a polite greeting can give away the register: Dear Mr Hill sounds formal, whereas Hiya sounds casual and friendly.

teaching.en: A contraction such as can't or I'd, together with slang like mate or cheers, makes a message sound relaxed, informal and personal.
teaching.es: Una contracción como can't o I'd, junto con jerga como mate o cheers, hace que un mensaje suene relajado, informal y personal.
teaching.explanationEs: Contracciones y jerga suman marcas informales; relaxed describe el tono resultante.
segments: A contraction such as can't or I'd, together with slang like
mate or cheers, makes a message sound relaxed, informal and personal.
teaching.audioText: A contraction such as can't or I'd, together with slang like mate or cheers, makes a message sound relaxed, informal and personal.

teaching.en: To sign off a formal email, write Kind regards or Yours sincerely; to sign off a note to a friend, Cheers or Speak soon is enough.
teaching.es: Para despedirte en un correo formal, escribe Kind regards o Yours sincerely; en una nota a un amigo basta con Cheers o Speak soon.
teaching.explanationEs: Sign off = cerrar el mensaje; el cierre debe coincidir con el registro del saludo.
segments: To sign off a formal email, write Kind regards or Yours sincerely; to
sign off a note to a friend, Cheers or Speak soon is enough.
teaching.audioText: To sign off a formal email, write Kind regards or Yours sincerely; to sign off a note to a friend, Cheers or Speak soon is enough.

teaching.en: Being polite is not the same as being formal: please and thank you suit every register, so a landlord can receive a friendly note that is still respectful.
teaching.es: Ser educado no es lo mismo que ser formal: please y thank you valen en cualquier registro, así que un casero puede recibir una nota amistosa y aun así respetuosa.
teaching.explanationEs: Polite ≠ formal: la cortesía existe en los dos registros.
segments: Being polite is not the same as being formal: please and thank you suit
every register, so a landlord can receive a friendly note that is still respectful.

prompt.es: Clasifica el mensaje y elige la marca que revela su registro.

choices.text: Formal: the request is direct, but it describes the heater in careful detail.
Informal, and therefore impolite, because slang can never be respectful.
Informal: Hiya, sort it out and Cheers show a relaxed register.

feedback.es: Hiya, sort it out y Cheers son marcas coloquiales; que haya jerga no vuelve grosero el mensaje.

hint.es: Mira el saludo, el verbo frasal y la despedida.

origin.text: Hiya Sam, the heater has packed up again, so can you sort it out before the weekend? It is really cold in here! Cheers, Mia

prompt.es: Completa: «Le agradecería que aceptara mi trabajo el viernes.»

feedback.es: I would be grateful if you could… es la fórmula formal estándar para pedir un favor por escrito.

origin.text: Dear Mrs Lee, I am writing about my essay. I would be ___ if you could accept it on Friday.

prompt.es: Ordena: «¿Puedes arreglar la calefacción antes del fin de semana?»

answer.text: Can you sort out the heater before the weekend
accepted: Can you sort out the heater before the weekend
Can you sort the heater out before the weekend

feedback.es: Can you + sort out es la petición coloquial; el verbo frasal puede separarse del objeto.

hint.es: Empieza con Can you y termina con weekend.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué cambió entre los dos mensajes de la compañera de piso.

choices.text: The register turned casual, although the problem stayed exactly the same.
Only the greeting changed, while the tone of the request stayed the same.
The heater got worse, so she chose a more formal register.

feedback.es: El problema es el mismo, pero el segundo mensaje pasa a un registro coloquial: no cambia solo el saludo ni se vuelve más formal.

origin.audio: My flatmate wrote two messages to our landlord about the same broken heater. The first began with Dear Mr Hill and politely asked, in full sentences without a single contraction, whether the repair could be done by Friday. The second, sent three days later, just said: Hiya, the heater has packed up again, sort it out, mate, cheers. Same flatmate, same problem, but the register changed completely, and I think the second message gave away how impatient she had become.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con la marca de registro que contiene.

pairs: Dear Mr Hill, I am writing to…
I'd sort it out if I were you.
I would be grateful if you could…

feedback.es: Cada frase contiene una marca distinta: saludo coloquial, apertura con apellido, verbo frasal o fórmula de petición.

pairs: Dear Mr Hill, I am writing to…
I'd sort it out if I were you.
I would be grateful if you could…

prompt.es: Escribe un correo formal: pides a Mr Hill que repare la calefacción.

answer.text: Dear Mr Hill, I would be grateful if you could repair the heater at your earliest convenience. Yours sincerely, Mia
accepted: Dear Mr Hill, I would be grateful if you could repair the heater at your earliest convenience. Yours sincerely, Mia
Dear Mr Hill, I would appreciate it if you could fix the heater as soon as possible. Kind regards, Mia
Dear Mr Hill, I would be grateful if you could arrange for the heater to be repaired at your earliest convenience. Kind regards, Mia

feedback.es: Un correo formal combina saludo con apellido, petición con would be grateful if you could y un cierre formal.

origin.text: Escribe a tu casero, Mr Hill: saludo formal, petición de que repare la calefacción cuanto antes y cierre formal.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué da a entender la hablante sobre el correo del cliente.

choices.text: It is formal throughout, so the casual phrase is fine.
It begins formally, but its register changes in the middle.
It is informal overall, apart from the greeting and closing.

feedback.es: La hablante dice que el registro «se desliza» a mitad del correo: apertura y cierre formales, pero una frase coloquial.

origin.audio: The client's email is strange. It opens with Dear Ms Novak, it has no contractions at all, and it ends with Yours sincerely. But right in the middle the writer says: could you sort it out by Friday, thanks? That casual phrase feels out of place, so I would say the tone changes halfway through.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez: ¿con qué propósito cita la hablante «sort it out»?

choices.text: To praise the natural, relaxed and friendly style of the writer.
To ask the client for a clearer request about the deadline.
To point out the phrase that breaks the formal tone.

feedback.es: Señala «sort it out» como la expresión que no encaja: su fin es localizar la ruptura del tono formal.

origin.audio: The client's email is strange. It opens with Dear Ms Novak, it has no contractions at all, and it ends with Yours sincerely. But right in the middle the writer says: could you sort it out by Friday, thanks? That casual phrase feels out of place, so I would say the tone changes halfway through.

prompt.es: Completa: «Una sola palabra de jerga puede delatar el registro real del autor.»

feedback.es: Give away significa revelar sin querer: una marca coloquial delata el registro que el autor intentaba ocultar.

origin.text: One slang word in an otherwise careful paragraph can ___ the writer's real register, however polite the rest of the message may sound.

prompt.es: Lee el aviso del casero: ¿qué actitud transmite su registro?

choices.text: He is polite but firm, and keeps a formal distance from her.
He is warm and relaxed, and treats her like an old friend.
He is sorry and unsure, and hopes she will not be upset.

feedback.es: El registro formal y la orden cortés (Please ensure…) marcan distancia y autoridad sin perder la educación.

origin.text: Dear Ms Green, further to my previous notice, I must remind you that the rent is due on the first of each month. Please make sure that payment is made on time. Yours sincerely, J. Hill

prompt.es: Tom escribe a Mia en tono coloquial: elige la respuesta que iguala su registro.

choices.text: Dear Tom, I am writing to confirm that I will attend the event.
Hey Tom! Yes, I'm coming, I'll be there by eight. See you!
Hello Tom. I would be grateful if you could save me a seat.

feedback.es: Con un amigo que escribe en coloquial, lo natural es responder con Hey, contracciones y un cierre breve.

origin.text: Tom has sent this to Mia: Hiya Mia! Are you coming to the party on Saturday? Don't be late, cheers! Mia wants to answer in the same register.

prompt.es: Completa: «Cada contracción, como I'm o don't, debe escribirse completa.»

feedback.es: I'm y don't son contracciones: en un texto formal se escriben I am y do not.

origin.text: In a letter to a landlord, each ___ such as I'm or don't should be written out in full, because the register must stay formal.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Empieza con Dear y termina con Yours sincerely.»

answer.text: Start with Dear and finish with Yours sincerely

feedback.es: La estructura del correo formal es saludo con Dear al principio y cierre al sign off con Yours sincerely.
